conventions.convention: Assume Countable Choice for the finite Fock, Fourier and tensor constructions. The dynamics and time-dependent Ward results additionally assume full Axiom of Choice through Stone's theorem.

The graph has finite nonempty vertex and link sets; parallel links and self-loops are allowed. There are s ≥ 1 modes per vertex, backgrounds b_x ∈ {0,…,s}, λ_E > 0, real plaquette coefficients, Hermitian onsite matrices and arbitrary complex hopping matrices.

Use second-variable-linear Hilbert pairings. Rotor angles lie in R/(2πZ), Haar measure is normalized by dθ/(2π), Fourier characters are exp(i Σ_e n_e θ_e), and E_e is the maximal diagonal multiplier n_e. The R/Z Fourier supplier is transferred by θ ↦ θ/(2π).

Occupation vectors use creators in increasing order of the fixed finite mode basis; the empty subset gives the vacuum. Number operators act by membership, and site number is the sum of its mode occupations.

G_x is outgoing electric flux minus incoming electric flux minus (n_x − b_x I), on its maximal diagonal domain. U(α) = exp(i Σ_x α_x G_x), so annihilation transforms by exp(iα_x) and a link unitary by exp(i(α_s − α_t)).
Evolution is exp(−itH/ℏ), with scalar ℏ > 0. Its infinitesimal generator is −iH/ℏ, and its self-adjoint Stone operator under the supplier's exp(itT) convention is −H/ℏ.
Boundary links have exactly one endpoint in R; their sign is +1 outward and −1 inward. The regional flux identity is asserted on physical vectors lying in every boundary electric-operator domain.

Time ordering puts larger times to the left, uses pairwise distinct insertion times and inserts no grading sign when moving G_x. Insertions are bounded, preserve D(G_x), and have bounded gauge-generator commutators.

The continuum localization clause is separate and conditional: a common invariant dense domain, smeared Gauss identity, electric locality outside compact K, bounded domain-preserving O, and the two stated strong limits are hypotheses; continuum existence is not concluded.

load_bearing.statement: Assuming Countable Choice, defines the finite oriented-graph rotor/CAR Hilbert space, joint Fourier/occupation basis, maximal electric and Gauss domains, fixed backgrounds, and H = H_0 + V_B + V_F on the displayed maximal electric-energy domain. The construction retains its conditional draft CAR input and assigns no physical units or continuum interpretation.

Assume Countable Choice, the stated finite-dimensional ordered orthonormal mode basis, antisymmetric Fock construction and CAR. Then the ordered occupation vectors ξ_S form an orthonormal basis; N_j is an orthogonal projection with N_j ξ_S = 1_{j∈S} ξ_S, and each site number is bounded self-adjoint with its stated occupation-count action.

For the conditional compact-rotor/CAR data, the maximal diagonal G_x are self-adjoint and strongly commute; U(α) is a strongly continuous torus representation with the displayed matter/link transformation laws. Its normalized Haar average is the orthogonal projection onto the joint Gauss kernel, which is nonzero for every admissible background.

Assume the model data. H_0 is nonnegative self-adjoint on the stated maximal diagonal domain with finite Fourier/occupation sums as graph core; V_B + V_F is bounded self-adjoint. H is self-adjoint on exactly D(H_0) and commutes with every gauge transformation on that domain.

Assume the model data and Axiom of Choice. For ℏ > 0, exp(−itH/ℏ) is a strongly continuous unitary group preserving D(H), with derivative −iH/ℏ there. It commutes with the gauge transformations and physical projection; its physical restriction has exact generator domain D(H) ∩ H_phys, and the restricted physical Hamiltonian is self-adjoint.
For R ⊆ V, on H_phys ∩ ⋂_{e∈∂R} D(E_e), the regional number Σ_{x∈R}(n_x − b_x I) equals Σ_{e∈∂R} ε(e,R)E_e. In particular, every physical vector has total occupation Σ_x b_x.

Under the finite model and Axiom of Choice, bounded gauge-charge eigenoperators and their finite products have zero physical expectation at nonzero total gauge charge. Domain-preserving bounded operators with bounded G_x commutators have zero physical commutator expectation. Evolution preserves gauge charge and D(G_x), so these assertions apply to the evolved operators.

published_dependencies.used_for: The explicit Countable Choice premise of the Hilbert tensor, finite Fock and Fourier constructions, and its relationship to the stronger AC assumption.
The full choice premise required by the cited Stone theorem and carried through dynamics and Ward results.
Hilbert tensor completion and completeness of product orthonormal bases, with explicit conjugation to the second-variable-linear convention.
Antisymmetrizing orthogonal projections, permutation action and vanishing of tensors with repeated factors in the occupation-basis proof.
Completeness of the rotor Fourier characters after the explicit measure-preserving conversion from R/(2πZ) to R/Z.
Existence, exact derivative domain and generator uniqueness for the global and restricted unitary groups, under AC and the exp(itT) sign convention.

alerts.finding: Facts & Assumptions [F3] attributes to lem-qft-lattice-physical-evolution that the restricted group 'has self-adjoint generator on D(H)∩H_phys'. The supplier's Statement instead explicitly gives the skew-adjoint infinitesimal generator −iH_phys/ℏ and the self-adjoint Stone operator −H_phys/ℏ. The consumer's Statement and conclusion correctly assert self-adjointness of H_phys, so this is a terminology/citation defect in [F3].

Opened the physical regulator postulate and both regulator theorems. Their graph, background, Hamiltonian domain, AC, Ward-domain and separate continuum hypotheses match the mathematical suppliers, and physical units are added explicitly.
